text: {"final": {"summary": "Created scripts/disburse_cycle2.py (P1): it loads active households via registry.register.load_households(active_only=True), checks eligibility with eligibility.rules.is_eligible (no score recomputation), and for each eligible household calls payments.vouchers.disburse(h.id, 60, payments.vouchers.payment_key(h.id, 2)) — no manual Payment construction or IDs. After a successful disbursement it queues a PAYMENT_SENT SMS via notifications.sms.queue_sms with {'amount': 60, 'cycle': 2, 'ref': payment.id}. No explicit now is passed, so config.settings.now() (2026-03-10T08:00:00) timestamps the records. DuplicatePayment is caught and skipped for idempotent re-runs, and the script prints the paid household IDs plus payments.receipts.total_paid() and per-household receipts_for(h.id) counts. Ran it once (P2): 16 eligible households (HH-10170, HH-10332, HH-10421, HH-10650, HH-11169, HH-12858, HH-13498, HH-13919, HH-14060, HH-14133, HH-14419, HH-14923, HH-15407, HH-16705, HH-16723, HH-16888) each received exactly one 60-dollar cycle-2 payment (keys HH-xxxx:2, PAY-00016..PAY-00031, sent_at 2026-03-10T08:00:00) and one PAYMENT_SENT SMS each. Verified in data/outbox/payments.jsonl: no ineligible household was paid, no household was paid twice for cycle 2, and total_paid of 1860 = 15 pre-existing cycle-1 payments (900) + 16 cycle-2 payments (960); HH-16723 is newly eligible in cycle 2 and correctly has only its cycle-2 payment.", "done_steps": ["P1", "P2"]}}
reasoning: The outbox shows cycle-1 payments existed before (15 payments, 1860 total = 15*60 + 16*60 = 900+960=1860). Wait, 16 cycle-2 payments × 60 = 960; cycle-1 had 15 × 60 = 900; total 1860. Correct. HH-16723 was newly eligible in cycle 2 (no cycle-1 payment). All 16 eligible households got exactly one cycle-2 payment of 60, timestamped 2026-03-10T08:00:00. No ineligible households paid. Done.
